question: A bus travelling at 95 km/hr completes a journey in 10 hours. What should be in its speed to cover the same distance in 5 hours?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Since the distance is constant, speed is inversely proportional to time.

Time ratio = 10 : 5 = 2 : 1

Speed ratio = 1 : 2

⇒ New Speed = 95 × 2 = 190 km/hr.

**∴ The correct answer is 190 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Initial speed of the bus (S₁) = 95 km/hr

Time taken (T₁) = 10 hours

New time (T₂) = 5 hours

**Formula Used:**

Distance = Speed &t
